Commentary.Commentary: Considering that there is an hour to go for the scheduled innings break, England will come out to bat till that time. How much will they score in this period? Can Australia pick up a wicket or two? The second question applies to the whole match looking at the way the English openers have batted in this series...

4 wickets for Moeen Ali - his career-best in ODIs. Does that come as a surprise? Not if you have followed England's bowling and Australia's batting in this series. He and Rashid finish with 12 wickets each - most by an English spinner in a bilateral ODI series. Sam Curran bowled well in his second spell while the others did decently in the limited opportunity they got.

Seemed like the Kangaroos were in for a big total when Finch and Head were going great guns. But then, after Finch got out, the Aussies slipped from 60/0 to 100/5. Alex Carey and D'Arcy Short then gave some hope to the tourists with a 59-run stand but the former's wicket just hastened the collapse. THIS IS THE THIRD SHORTEST INNINGS FOR AUSTRALIA IN ODIS AFTER BATTING FIRST.

208 legal balls - that is all it has taken for England to dismantle Australia. On a very good track for batting, the visitors have just thrown away their wickets, as if not seemingly interested in playing at all. The openers started off in a hurry - then the rest followed them in a hurry - but back to the pavillion.
OUT! BOWLED! No half century for Short. A long hop, Stanlake goes back to pull but misses and the ball skids through to hit the leg stump! ENGLAND NEED 206 FOR A 5-0 WHITEWASH!!!
Full on middle and leg, defended to the leg side.
Outside off, crunched through the covers for a single.
FOUR! MURDERED! Tossed up on middle, Short comes down the track and lofts it over the bowler for a boundary!
Down the leg side, Stanlake looks to flick but the ball lobs off the pads and Buttler grabs it. They appeal for the catch but there was no bat there.
Action replay of the previous delivery.
The googly, around off, Stanlake pushes but misses.
200 UP FOR AUSTRALIA! Ironic cheers from the crowd. Down the leg side once more, D'Arcy sweeps it powerfully towards Jonny Bairstow at deep backward square leg and nearly holes out. A single taken.
WIDE. Down the leg side, Short looks to sweep but misses.
Outside off, driven towards short extra cover where Eoin Morgan dives to his left but parries it towards long off. A single taken.
Full and around middle, worked towards mid-wicket.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Punches this off the back foot again.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
The batsman dances down the track. One run added to the total.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
Moeen Ali is back on. He has never got a 4-fer in ODI cricket...
On middle and leg, worked towards square leg.
Lunges to this one and pushes it towards point.
Full and around leg stump, defended back to the bowler.
Billy Stanlake is the last man in. Can he hang around for Short's fifty? Not that it matters anyways...

OUT! Stone dead. A short ball, on off, the googly, skids through. Lyon looks to pull but misses and is hit right in front. He starts walking off after the umpire raises his finger but Short asks him to wait and signals for the review. Well, Lyon does not have to wait for long. The Hawk Eye quickly indicates that he is dead in front.
Now Australia take a review. Lyon seems to be plumb in front...
Full on middle, flicked through mid-wicket and now he takes the single.
Full and outside off, driven towards long off. SINGLE NOT TAKEN.
Make that a hat-trick of plays and misses to end the over.
Outside off, angling away, another play and a miss from Nathan.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball - but fails.
Whips this over mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Stand and deliver! Outside off, Short stands tall and punches it through the covers for a boundary!

HOWZZAT? Not out. Full and down the leg side, Short misses his flick and there is a noise as the ball goes through to Buttler. England go up again but this time the umpire shakes his head. Replays indicate no bat, only pad.

NOT OUT! England exhaust their only review. Full and outside off, Lyon looked to go for his favourite shot - the sweep - only to miss. The ball went off his pads to Joe Root at first slip who went up in an appeal. England were supremely confident and seeing that Morgan signalled a 'T'. Now, when the ball passed the bat, the Snickometer seemed to suggest a deviation. Was that the outside edge? Or was that the bat hitting the ground? The third umpire had quite a few to and fros before eventually getting convinced there was no outside edge. He then checked for the customary Ball Tracking and the impact was OUTSIDE OFF.
Caught at slip? No, says Dharmasena. England want it reviewed...
Goes for another sweep but misses and is hit on the pads.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.
Full toss outside off, Lyon gets down and sweeps it through square leg for a single.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, Lyon pushes but misses.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Pushes this through mid on for a quick single.
Clips it through mid-wicket for a couple.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Nathan Lyon walks in at number 10, replacing Richardson.

OUT! Yes, that is the second run out of the game. On middle and leg, Richardson works it wide of short fine leg and sets off for a single. Short does not agree and sends his partner back. Kane could have still got back but he stops for a second, as if in disbelief. Then looks to go back. By that time the throw comes in to Buttler from Moeen who collects it in front of his stumps then whips them from behind. Richardson puts in a dive and it is referred upstairs and the first replay makes it clear, though the third umpire takes a lot of replays to confirm...
Another run out? Seems to be so! Buttler is confident again and it is referred upstairs...
SIX! He has hit that alright. Full and outside off, Richardson slogs it over wide mid on and the ball clears the ropes!
Around middle and off, defended back to the bowler.
Full around middle, watchfully defended.
Outside off, Richardson slogs it over mid-wicket for a couple.
Full and down the leg side, swept through fine leg for a single.
Pushes this wide of mid on for a quick run.
Fuller, driven back to the bowler.
FOUR! Fine shot. On a length outside off, Short flays this behind point and gets a boundary. The stand moves to 12 from 13 balls.

DIRECT HIT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT SHORT SHORT. Outside off, Richardson taps it towards point and the batsmen go for a suicidal single. Jason Roy, fields, takes aim and then has a shy at the striker's end but misses. D'Arcy was nowhere in the frame.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
The batsman gets an inside edge and the ball hits him on the pads. They pick up a single.
A short ball, Kane looks to pull but misses. The ball stays low and Buttler fumbles.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, defended watchfully.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

DROPPED! Tough chance but did Plunkett make that look difficult? Full and outside off, Richardson looks to go big but skews it off the outer half. The ball goes towards cover but Liam Plunkett at mid off takes a late start. Probably that goes against him as he does get to the ball, sticks out his left hand but the ball brushes his fingertips and goes down. A couple taken.

The batsman plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. One run added to the total. 4 runs and 2 wickets from the over - Curran's figures now read 3-0-29-2. This is some achievement for Australia considering their batting in this match - they have managed to last the halfway mark with the bat.
WIDE. A bouncer on middle, Richardson ducks. The umpire signals a wide for height.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads for a couple.
Around middle and off, watchfully defended.
Kane Richardson walks in at number 9, replacing Agar.

OUT! Agar's stumps and Australia - both are in a mess. Total loss of judgement. Curran lands this on a length in line of the stumps and Agar - for reasons known only to him, shoulders arms. Did he expect the ball to go over the sticks? Well, the ball just went straight through and shattered the timber. A 2-ball duck for Agar.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Ashton Agar walks in at number 8, replacing Carey.

OUT! Maiden ODI wicket for the debutant as he strikes on the very first ball of his second spell! Not the greatest of balls but the youngster will not mind. He lands this on a length outside off, pretty harmless and Carey tries to be cheeky, aiming to run this towards third man. Only manages a thin outside edge which goes straight to Jos Buttler. Another promising innings from an Aussie batsman cut short. The stand was decent too - 59 from 60 balls.
Sam Curran is back on. 2-0-25-0 so far.
Another sweep, this time towards Jonny Bairstow at deep square leg for a run. 10 from the over, 24 off the last 2!
FOUR! Powerfully swept! Full and down the leg side, Carey sweeps it to the fine leg fence!
Full on middle, driven back to the bowler.
The googly, around off, pushed through the covers for a couple.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On middle and leg, Short whips it through mid-wicket where Alex Hales does well to save the boundary. Three runs taken. 150 UP FOR AUSTRALIA and it also raises the 50-run stand between these two.

FOUR! 10 from the last 2 balls! Wide outside off, Carey flays it through the covers and gets a boundary! 14 from that over. Kumar Sangakkara with a fine comment on air - 'Good signs for Australia but ominous signs considering England's batting line-up on this good-looking pitch'. True...

SIX! IMPERIOUS! Full and around middle, Carey comes forward and lofts it nonchalantly down the ground, just in front of the sightscreen! Moves to 31 from 33 balls. The stand is worth 45 from 52 balls.
Short and outside off, cut through the covers for another single.
Full and down the leg side, swept fine for one.
Pushes this through mid on for a run.

TROUBLE, SAFE! Full on middle, Carey works it towards mid-wicket and takes a single. He turns for the second and almost reaches halfway before he is sent back. Dives in the nick of time before Root disturbs the bails.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full and around off, D'Arcy looks to go over mid off but skews it in the air. It lands just short of Jake Ball at mid off.
Short and outside off, punched towards short mid-wicket.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Full and around off, driven towards mid off.
Full and around leg, swept through fine leg for a single.
Looks to tuck it to the leg side but the ball dips on him and goes off the leading edge to point. A run taken.
Waits for the ball to come to him and plays it extremely late, from the stumps towards short third man. Just a single for all that risk.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for another one.
On middle and leg, flicked away for a run.
Pushes this towards long on for a single.
Misses out. Full and down the leg side, Short gets down and sweeps it straight to Adil Rashid at short fine leg.
Joe Root is back on. Went for 13 in his solitary over.
Full and around middle, Alex uses his wrists and flicks it straight to short mid-wicket.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Another wrong 'un, short and outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
The leggie now, from the leggie, on middle and leg, Short lunges and defends.
On middle and leg, swept towards fine leg for a single.
The googly to start. Around off, driven straight to cover.
Adil Rashid finally comes into the attack.
Full and outside off, Carey leans and drives it through mid off for a run.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Short and outside off, punched towards cover.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. Two runs added to the total.
Around off, defended watchfully.
Goes hard at this one as well, without moving his feet and gets a thick inside edge past the stumps towards short fine leg. A run taken.
FOUR! In the air, but wide! Full and outside off, Short throws the kitchen sink at it and just about gets it past Joe Root at short extra cover for a boundary!
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Fuller and around off, defended towards cover.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, punched straight to point.

DRINKS BREAK. You know, this series reminds me of my childhood days. I used to watch serials during the week and when I missed any episode, then I used to catch the repeat telecast on a Sunday. In every match of the series, or rather most, Australia have raced off to a start, only to capitulate after that. Today seems no different. 60/0 at one stage and then 100/5. Justin Langer has a lot of work to do...
Pushes this through mid off for a run.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
On middle and leg, whipped through mid-wicket for a run.
FOUR! Interesting! Full and outside off, Carey gets across and attempts the paddle scoop. Buttler gets across to his right but the ball goes past his left hand and into the fine leg fence!
Fuller, whipped past Morgan at short mid-wicket for a couple. The stand moves to 11 from 13 balls.
FOUR! HAMMERED! Full and outside off, Carey gets down and mows it over mid-wicket for a boundary! Moves to 13 from 18 balls with his second boundary.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
It's been driven superbly through the covers.
On a length outside off, dabbed to third man for a run.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
WIDE. Way down the leg side, Short lets it go.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, Carey slashes hard and gets a thick outside edge to third man for a single.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
The batsman gets an inside edge and the ball hits him on the pads.
Punches this off the back foot.
Full and outside off, driven towards cover.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
D'Arcy Short walks in at number 7, replacing Paine. Australia will hope it is a long innings...

OUT! It is pain for Paine and Australia! Half the side is back in the hut and we are not even into the first Drinks Break. Around middle and leg, Paine just tucks it to the leg side and the batsmen attempt a quick single. Jos Buttler rushes to the ball, picks it up, is off balance, but still manages to throw it to the bowler's end and voila! Bull's Eye! As they say, when nothing is going for you, NOTHING INDEED IS GOING FOR YOU. Normally, on another day, Buttler would have stumbled, taken extra time, perhaps slipped or maybe, missed the stumps. But what he does instead is hand an unwanted record for Paine - WORST BATTING AVERAGE IN AN ODI SERIES IN ENGLAND BY AN AUSTRALIAN CAPTAIN (MINIMUM 3 INNINGS)!!!
Direct hit! Is it pain for Paine? Referred upstairs...
Around middle and leg, tucked to the leg side.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Outside off, tapped towards point for a quick run.
WIDE. Down the leg side, Paine misses his flick.
Full and outside off, sliced through point for a single.
Around middle, Carey plays that with a loose bottom hand and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. Plunkett is mainly bowling cutters here.
A bouncer around middle and leg, defended watchfully.
Tim Paine walks in at number 6, replacing Marsh.

OUT! What a ball, what a piece of stumping! Marsh is outta here! It is not raining in Old Trafford but Australia are amidst old pools of trouble. Moeen tosses this up beautifully outside off and gets Marsh drawn forward. The southpaw lunges to defend but then the ball drifts away, beating the bat. Now, because of that lunge, Shaun's back foot is in the air. Jos Buttler collects and then whips the bails off in a flash! He appeals confidently and when it is taken upstairs, the first replay confirms his ecstasy. Australia so far - Head - 56 and the other three have played like a tail - 22 (Finch), 8 (Marsh) and 0 (Stoinis).
Is Marsh stumped? Buttler certainly seems confident! Referred upstairs...
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
WIDE. Miles outside off, spinning away, let through.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
FOUR! Nice shot. Confident-looking one. Full on middle, Carey gets down and reverse sweeps it behind point for a boundary to get going!
Full and around middle, watchfully defended.
Outside off, punched down to long on for a single.
On a length outside off, Alex lets that carry through to the keeper. 7 runs and a wicket from Plunkett's opening over.
Alex Carey walks in at number 5, replacing Head.

OUT! Another soft dismissal. Commentator's curse. Just a few balls ago, on his half century, we had mentioned that Head had failed to convert his start in the previous game. Today, he is playing with a cool head. Well... he has chipped a length delivery straight into Eoin Morgan's hands at short mid-wicket. Australia rise high... only to sink lower...
FOUR! Down the leg side, Head tickles it fine past the keeper to the fine leg fence.
Outside off, played straight to point.

LUCKY... Plunkett lands it on a length on middle, Shaun looks to defend but with lazy feet movement. The ball comes back in, takes the inside edge and goes past the stumps towards short fine leg. A single taken.
Full on middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a couple.
Liam Plunkett to bowl his first now.
Full and around off, Marsh stays leg side of the ball and drives it inside out wide of long off for another single.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Outside off, punched off the back foot through sweeper cover for one.
On middle and leg, tucked through square leg for a run.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and around off, defended watchfully by Head coming down the track.
POWERPLAY 2 time. 4 fielders allowed outside the 30-yard circle, till the 40th over.

The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. 79/2 in POWERPLAY 1 for Australia - Pretty decent as has been in most games in this series - it is from here that they have gone into a shell.

HALF CENTURY FOR HEAD! He threw his start away in Durham but so far, Travis has played with a cool head. Wickets have been falling at the other end but TH has been playing his own game at this end. A length ball around middle, Head waits for the ball to come to him and guides it deftly to third man for a run. 10th half century in this format, third in succession.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads for a single.
On middle and leg, tucked through square leg for a run.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
FOUR! Short and wide outside off, Head rocks back and cuts it through point for a boundary.
Comes down the track and drives it through mid off for a run.
Around off, defended watchfully.

Mid off goes back now. Square leg comes inside the circle. Very good captaincy from Morgan, comments Ricky Ponting on air. Punter opines that Morgan knows that Head is good down the ground and with the sweep shot. Hence the field change.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single. Gets off the mark.
Punches it wide of mid off for a quick single.

FOUR! Nicely done. Comes down the track, gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it past the bowler, down the ground and the timing is good enough to beat mid off. Moves to 42 from 29 balls with his seventh boundary.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Around middle and off, defended watchfully.

LUCKY! The off cutter, on middle and leg, TH is early into his flick and gets a leading edge. Luckily for him, the ball balloons over the bowler and lands in no man's land between mid on and mid off! A single taken.
A length ball, around middle and leg, Travis waits for the ball to come to him and helps it towards short fine leg.
Full and outside off, pushed uppishly but the ball does not carry to the man at cover.
FOUR! PRISTINE! Full and outside off, Head leans into this one and drives it through the covers for a boundary! The stand gets off the mark.
On middle and off, driven towards cover.
On middle and leg, helped towards short fine leg. 2 singles, 2 dots and 2 wicket-dot balls in that over. Superb start from Moeen.
Shaun Marsh comes in at number 4, replacing Stoinis.

OUT! Straight to the man and Moeen has two in the over! Stoinis has come and Stoinis has gone. And the over is not yet over. A nothing delivery, a nothing shot. The bowler wins, though. Full and around off, Marcus gets down on a knee and looks to sweep it over the man at short fine leg. But all he does is - hit it straight to Jake Ball over there. He is one of the tallest men in the England line-up and perhaps a shorter guy would have missed it. Not Ball, who gobbles the ball. First duck in ODIs for Stoinis!!!
Full and outside off, defended towards mid on.
Oho! Interesting! Marcus Stoinis has been promoted to number 3, replacing Finch.

OUT! Chops it on! Once again, a start is wasted by an Aussie batsman. A short ball outside off, Finch goes back to pull but the ball stays low, takes the inner half of the bat and uproots the leg stump! A decent start by Finch but then, he could have carried on longer. Throws his wicket away.
Comes down the track but is beaten in flight. Somehow, Head manages to get the ball away through the covers for a single.

A reverse sweep employed straightaway. But it was risky. He was early into the shot, Finch and the ball went off the back of his bat towards short fine leg. There was a muted LBW appeal and rightly, not reviewed. A single taken.
Another change of bowling. Moeen Ali into the attack.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.

DROPPED? Or short? Need more replays to look at that. Finch tucks this length ball uppishly towards short fine leg where Sam Curran dives but is not able to hold on. Now, one angle seems to show that the ball burst through his fingers while another seems to show that the ball landed in front.
On middle and leg, tucked behind square leg for a single.

FOUR! Stand and deliver! Not a bad ball at all. He lands this on a length outside off but Head plays a lovely shot, driving this on the up. This time, the timing is excellent to beat the man at short extra cover. Moves to 31 from 20 balls with his 5th boundary.
Full and around off, driven straight to short extra cover.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Change of ends for Jake Ball.
Fuller and wider outside off, this time Aaron goes hard and skews it off the outer half over cover. Two runs taken. 13 from the over, 24 off the last 2!

FOUR! FETCH THAT! Full on middle and leg, Finch backs away to the leg side and clobbers the ball straight back over Root's head, a bounce and into the ropes! Back-to-back 50-stands for the Aussie openers!
Now this is fuller on the pads, flicked towards short fine leg for a quick single.

FOUR! Bad ball. That is because of Head's footwork. On seeing Travis step out on the first two balls, Root drops this short and wide outside off. This time though, the batsman stays in his crease and cuts it behind point for a boundary.
Comes out again and chips this towards long on where Alex Hales makes a good tumbling stop. Two runs taken. The stand is worth 41 from 26 balls.
Tossed up around off, Head is straightaway down the track but is not to the pitch of the ball. Has to defend.
Early change for England. Joe Root to bowl now.
Full again, driven towards mid off. 11 from the over, Curran has gone for 25 in his 2 overs.
Around off, defended solidly.

SIX! Not cleanly hit but the bat is so solid that the ball will travel. Curran goes fuller and lines this just around off stump. But Finch is in no mood to defend and swings across the line. The ball hits the inner half of the bat, but still travels way over mid-wicket! Finch moves to 14 from 9 balls.

FOUR! Up and over! No need to run for that. A hat-trick of length balls, outside off, angling away and this time, Finch is ready. Comes forward and lofts it over extra cover for a boundary. The stand is worth 33 from 21 balls.
Ooh... nearly chased that. A length ball once more, angling away outside off, Finch pushes but misses.
A length ball down the leg side, tucked towards fine leg for a single. Head moves to 20 from 13 balls.

FOUR! Now he gets off the mark and in some style too! Full around off, swinging in, Finch covers the line nicely and works it wide of mid on. The timing is good enough and it will beat the fielder to the fence.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off for a quick single.

FOUR! Easy pickings. Ball strays on the pads and all Head has to do is to go back and whip the ball through square leg for a boundary. Nicely timed. The stand moves to 23 from 16 balls. Finch is yet to score a run.
On middle once more, blocked from the crease.
Full on middle, Head drives this straight back. Starts to run on seeing that the ball has not been properly fielded by Ball but then has to go back seeing mid on charge in.
On a length around leg and middle, defended from the crease.

Full on middle, Travis drives it straight down the ground. Moeen Ali dives to his right from mid on but is not able to stop it cleanly. Parries it towards the boundary. However, takes some pace off it and hence mid off is able to get around and slide to parry the ball back to Moeen. Three runs taken. 14 from Sam Curran's opening over.
FOUR! More wrong line. On the pads, this time Head does not miss out and whips it behind square leg for a boundary. The man at the ropes is in front of square and cannot get there in time.
On middle and leg, tucked through square leg for a couple.
WIDE. Slips this down the leg side, Travis misses his flick. The bowler might consider himself lucky there - fine leg was up.
Full and around off, stoutly blocked away.
FOUR! Not a bad ball at all. Plenty of swing, shaping away, a low full toss but Head plays this nicely, driving the ball through cover and point. First boundary of Sunday.
Around off, defended back  to the bowler.
Debutant Sam Curran, 250th player to represent England in ODI cricket, will bowl with the second new ball.
Around off, angling in, defended back to the bowler.
One more delivery down the leg side, tucked towards fine leg for a single. Head gets off the mark.

Good stop by Adil Rashid in the deep. Down the leg side, AF misses his tuck and the ball goes off his pads towards fine leg. Rashid gives it a good chase from backward square leg and dives to pull the ball back in. Three runs taken.
More inswing, well bowled and equally well played. Driven towards mid on.
Full and outside off, hint of inswing, Aaron drives it straight back and Ball stops it in his followthrough, albeit not cleanly.
Outside off, this is well inside the guideline, left alone and not wided.

WIDE. A harsh call from the umpire, one might argue. Full and outside off, in line of the wide guideline, Finch shoulders arms. The umpire stretches his arms and the bowler is surprised. Replays show that the ball just grazed the guideline. Maybe, some leniency could have been shown. Strict umpire.
The players are out in the middle! Travis Head and Aaron Finch are the openers. Jake Ball will bowl with the first new ball to Finch. Here we go...

England team changes - Three for them today. Sam Curran, Jake Ball and Liam Plunkett get an opportunity in place of David Willey, Mark Wood and the injured Craig Overton. SAM CURRAN IS JUST THE SECOND YOUNGEST PLAYER TO MAKE AN ODI DEBUT FOR ENGLAND. Aged 20 years and 21 days, he gets the cap from James Anderson.

Australian team changes - Seems like it was a short stay on the bench and D'Arcy is back in the playing XI. So is Kane Richardson. Out go Jhye Richardson and Michael Neser. Glenn Maxwell still has a sore shoulder by the looks of it and will not play again.

TOSS - Australia have whitewashed England! Congratulations to them!!! Ah... ok... forgot that a cricket match is never won purely on toss (except in certain conditions where rain is involved and it is a knockout game). To cut matters short, Tim Paine has won his 5th toss in a row in this series and once again, AUSTRALIA WILL BAT FIRST.

WEATHER - How is it? Well, nice, bright and sunny. No chances of rain. Plus, the expectations are that of the pitch getting drier as the game progresses, so the captain winning the toss will like to bat first.

An Aussie fan? Don't blame you for thinking - 'Another Sunday wasted...' English fan? You might already be thinking - 'Forget the Aussies.. let us sound a warning to India!' Either ways, people would be more interested in the FIFA World Cup where England play Panama in the first game of the day. But the hosts have a big record to chase in cricket today - They have never whitewashed the Aussies in this format and that is a good dangling carrot. For the visiting side, well, it is nothing more than pride. They were whitewashed by South Africa in late 2016 and they certainly will hope that today is not another of 'those' days. Hello and a warm welcome to the fifth and final ODI between England and Australia at Old Trafford, Manchester.
